source.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν τῷ τὸν ὄχλον ἐπικεῖσθαι αὐτῷ καὶ ἀκούειν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν ἑστὼς παρὰ τὴν λίμνην Γεννησαρὲτ, καὶ εἶδεν δύο πλοῖα ἑστῶτα παρὰ τὴν λίμνην, οἱ δὲ ἁλιεῖς ἀπ’ αὐτῶν ἀποβάντες ἔπλυνον τὰ δίκτυα.

records.literal_gloss: It came to pass then in the the crowd to press upon him and to hear the word of the God, and he was standing beside the lake Gennesaret, \v 2 and he saw two boats standing beside the lake; the and fishermen from them having gone out were washing the nets.

en.L: And it happened, while the crowd was pressing on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and hearing the word of God, that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret, \v 2 and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw two boats standing beside the lake; but the fishermen had gone out of them and were washing the nets.
en.B: Once, as Jesus stood beside the lake of Gennesaret, the crowd was pushing in around {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to hear the word of God. \v 2 He noticed two boats drawn up at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had climbed out of them and were washing their nets.
en.R: One day Jesus was standing on the shore of Lake Gennesaret. A crowd of people was pushing close to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to listen to God's message. \v 2 Jesus saw two boats at the edge of the lake. The fishermen had left their boats and were washing their nets.

es.L: Y sucedió que, mientras la multitud se apretujaba sobre {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y oía la palabra de Dios, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba de pie junto al lago de Genesaret, \v 2 y vio dos barcas que estaban junto al lago; pero los pescadores habían bajado de ellas y lavaban las redes.
es.B: Una vez, mientras Jesús estaba de pie a la orilla del lago de Genesaret, la multitud se agolpaba a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor para oír la palabra de Dios. \v 2 Vio dos barcas arrimadas a la orilla del lago. Los pescadores habían bajado de ellas y estaban lavando sus redes.
es.R: Un día Jesús estaba en la orilla del lago de Genesaret. Mucha gente se apretaba a {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} alrededor para escuchar el mensaje de Dios. \v 2 Jesús vio dos barcas en la orilla del lago. Los pescadores habían salido de ellas y estaban lavando sus redes.

sw.L: Ikawa, umati ulipokuwa ukimsonga na kulisikia neno la Mungu, {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa amesimama kando ya ziwa la Genesareti, \v 2 akaona mashua mbili zimesimama kando ya ziwa; lakini wavuvi walikuwa wameshuka kutoka ndani yake, wakiosha nyavu.
sw.B: Siku moja Yesu alipokuwa amesimama kando ya ziwa la Genesareti, umati wa watu ulikuwa ukimsonga ili kulisikia neno la Mungu. \v 2 Akaona mashua mbili zimekaa ukingoni mwa ziwa. Wavuvi walikuwa wametoka ndani yake, wakiosha nyavu zao.
sw.R: Siku moja Yesu alikuwa amesimama ufuoni mwa Ziwa Genesareti. Watu wengi walikuwa wakimsonga ili wasikilize ujumbe wa Mungu. \v 2 Yesu aliona mashua mbili ukingoni mwa ziwa. Wavuvi walikuwa wameziacha mashua zao, nao walikuwa wakiosha nyavu zao.

decisions.choice: the lake of Gennesaret: the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Gennesaret was the fertile plain on the north-west shore of the lake, and the lake was also called by its name. Mark and Matthew call it the Sea of Galilee (Mark 1:16); John calls it the Sea of Tiberias (John 21:1). Luke always calls it a lake (8:22-23).

decisions.choice: the word of God: Jesus's teaching, which is God's message
decisions.reason: Luke uses the phrase for the message Jesus proclaims (8:11, 21) and later for the message the apostles preach (Acts 4:31; 6:2).

decisions.choice: washing the nets: cleaning and mending them after a night's work
decisions.reason: Fishermen on the lake worked with nets at night (5:5) and cleaned them in the morning, so that weed and mud would not rot them.

decisions.choice: Jesus (B, R); he (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section of the story.

decisions.choice: God's message
decisions.reason: Readable says what "the word" means here.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives (él, lo, le, su, tu, ti), not on verb endings (estaba, vio)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("sígueme"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English, as in Mark 2. This holds for the whole chapter.

decisions.choice: el lago (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke's own word here is "lake" (meaning decision m1), not the "sea" of Matthew and Mark, so even Literal says "lago".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on verb prefixes (ukimsonga, alikuwa); spans only on free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, yake, nawe)
decisions.reason: The English "him" and "he" take the setting. Swahili carries them in the verb prefixes, which cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark 2. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: ziwa (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke's own word here is "lake" (meaning decision m1), not the "sea" of Matthew and Mark, so even Literal says "ziwa".

source.text: ἐμβὰς δὲ εἰς ἓν τῶν πλοίων, ὃ ἦν Σίμωνος, ἠρώτησεν αὐτὸν ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἐπαναγαγεῖν ὀλίγον, καθίσας δὲ ἐκ τοῦ πλοίου ἐδίδασκεν τοὺς ὄχλους.

records.literal_gloss: Having entered then into one of the boats, which was of Simon, he asked him from the land to put out a little; having sat down then out of the boat he was teaching the crowds.

en.L: And getting into one of the boats, which was Simon's, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} asked him to put out a little from the land; and sitting down, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching the crowds from the boat.
en.B: He got into one of the boats, the one that belonged to Simon, and asked him to push off a short way from the shore. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down and taught the crowds from the boat.
en.R: Jesus got into one of the boats. It belonged to Simon. Jesus asked Simon to push the boat out a little way from the shore. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sat down in the boat and taught the people.

es.L: Y subiendo a una de las barcas, que era de Simón, le pidió que se apartara un poco de la tierra; y sentándose, enseñaba a las multitudes desde la barca.
es.B: Subió a una de las barcas, la que era de Simón, y le pidió que la alejara un poco de la orilla. Luego se sentó y enseñaba a la multitud desde la barca.
es.R: Jesús subió a una de las barcas. Era de Simón. Jesús le pidió a Simón que alejara la barca un poco de la orilla. Luego se sentó en la barca y enseñó a la gente.

sw.L: Akiisha kupanda katika mojawapo ya mashua, iliyokuwa ya Simoni, alimwomba aisogeze mbali kidogo kutoka nchi kavu; na akiketi, alikuwa akiwafundisha makundi ya watu kutoka ndani ya mashua.
sw.B: Alipanda katika mojawapo ya mashua, ile iliyokuwa ya Simoni, akamwomba aisukume mbali kidogo kutoka ufuoni. Kisha akaketi, akawafundisha makundi ya watu akiwa ndani ya mashua.
sw.R: Yesu alipanda katika mojawapo ya mashua. Ilikuwa mali ya Simoni. Yesu akamwomba Simoni aisogeze mashua mbali kidogo na ufuo. Kisha akaketi ndani ya mashua, akawafundisha watu.

decisions.choice: having sat down: Jewish teachers usually sat to teach
decisions.reason: Jesus sat down to teach in the synagogue at Nazareth (4:20), as teachers did. From the boat he could see the whole crowd on the shore.

decisions.choice: Simon: the man whose mother-in-law Jesus has already healed
decisions.reason: Jesus has been in Simon's house in Capernaum (4:38-39). Luke introduces him by his own name; Jesus will name him Peter (6:14).

decisions.choice: barca
decisions.reason: A small open fishing boat. "Barco" suggests a larger ship; "bote" is regional. The same through the chapter.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἐπαύσατο λαλῶν, εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα· Ἐπανάγαγε εἰς τὸ βάθος καὶ χαλάσατε τὰ δίκτυα ὑμῶν εἰς ἄγραν.

records.literal_gloss: When then he stopped speaking, he said to the Simon, Put out into the deep and let down the nets of you for a catch.

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} stopped speaking, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Simon, "Put out into the deep [water], and let down your nets for a catch."
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had finished speaking, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} told Simon, "Take the boat out where the water is deep, and lower your nets to catch fish."
en.R: When Jesus finished teaching, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to Simon, "Take the boat out into deep water. Then put your nets down into the water to catch some fish."

es.L: Y cuando dejó de hablar, dijo a Simón: «Lleva [la barca] a lo hondo, y {{plural_you:echen|echad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} redes para pescar».
es.B: Cuando terminó de hablar, le dijo a Simón: «Lleva la barca adonde el agua es profunda, y {{plural_you:echen|echad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} redes para pescar».
es.R: Cuando Jesús terminó de enseñar, le dijo a Simón: «Lleva la barca a aguas profundas. Luego {{plural_you:echen|echad}} {{plural_you:sus|vuestras}} redes al agua para pescar».

sw.L: Na alipomaliza kusema, alimwambia Simoni, "Peleka [mashua] kilindini, na mshushe nyavu zenu kwa ajili ya kuvua."
sw.B: Alipokwisha kusema, alimwambia Simoni, "Ipeleke mashua mahali penye kina kirefu, kisha mshushe nyavu zenu mvue samaki."
sw.R: Yesu alipomaliza kufundisha, alimwambia Simoni, "Ipeleke mashua kwenye maji yenye kina kirefu. Kisha mshushe nyavu zenu majini ili mvue samaki."

decisions.choice: put out (to Simon alone), let down your nets (to Simon and his crew)
decisions.reason: The first verb is singular and the second is plural. Simon steers the boat; the whole crew handles the nets.

decisions.choice: deep water by day: against the fishermen's experience
alternatives: the usual time and place to fish
decisions.reason: Fishermen on the lake worked through the night (5:5). Simon's answer shows that he did not expect a catch.

decisions.choice: to catch fish
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name what is caught.

decisions.choice: lleva (to Simon, singular, no span); echen|echad, sus|vuestras (to the crew, plural_you spans)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks first to Simon alone, then to Simon and his crew (meaning decision m1); Spanish shows the change in the verb. The plural forms take the plural_you setting, which chooses between Latin American "ustedes" and Peninsular "vosotros"; English has no such choice. The same throughout the chapter.

decisions.choice: peleka (singular, to Simon); mshushe, zenu (plural, to the crew)
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks first to Simon alone, then to Simon and his crew (meaning decision m1). Swahili verbs and possessives show singular and plural as the Greek does, so the change comes through without any setting.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς Σίμων εἶπεν· Ἐπιστάτα, δι’ ὅλης νυκτὸς κοπιάσαντες οὐδὲν ἐλάβομεν, ἐπὶ δὲ τῷ ῥήματί σου χαλάσω τὰ δίκτυα.

records.literal_gloss: And answering Simon said, Master, through whole night having toiled nothing we took; at but the word of you I will let down the nets.

en.L: And Simon answered and said, "Master, we toiled through [the] whole night and took nothing, but at {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I will let down the nets."
en.B: Simon replied, "Master, we worked hard the whole night through and caught nothing. But on {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word I will lower the nets."
en.R: Simon answered, "Master, we worked hard all night, and we did not catch a thing. But {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} told me to do it, so I will put the nets down."

es.L: Y respondiendo Simón, dijo: «Maestro, habiendo trabajado duro durante toda [la] noche, no sacamos nada; pero por {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} palabra echaré las redes».
es.B: Simón le respondió: «Maestro, hemos trabajado duro toda la noche y no hemos pescado nada. Pero, como {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} lo mandas, echaré las redes».
es.R: Simón contestó: «Maestro, trabajamos mucho toda la noche y no pescamos nada. Pero {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} me dices que lo haga, así que echaré las redes».

sw.L: Na Simoni akajibu, akasema, "Mkuu, tukiwa tumetaabika usiku wote hatukupata chochote; lakini kwa neno {{deity_pronoun:lako|Lako}} nitazishusha nyavu."
sw.B: Simoni alijibu, "Mkuu, tumefanya kazi kwa bidii usiku kucha, wala hatukupata kitu. Lakini kwa kuwa {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umesema, nitazishusha nyavu."
sw.R: Simoni alijibu, "Mkuu, tulifanya kazi kwa bidii usiku wote, lakini hatukupata samaki hata mmoja. Lakini {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} umeniambia nifanye hivyo, kwa hiyo nitazishusha nyavu."

decisions.choice: Master: one who has authority and gives orders
decisions.reason: Only Luke uses this word in the New Testament, and always for Jesus, mostly on the lips of his disciples (8:24, 45; 9:33). It was used of an overseer or commander. Simon will soon call Jesus "Lord" (5:8).

decisions.choice: your word: your command
decisions.reason: The noun means a spoken word. Simon obeys an order that goes against his experience.

decisions.choice: toiled: worked to the point of weariness
decisions.reason: The verb means hard, tiring work.

decisions.choice: you told me to do it, so I will put the nets down
alternatives: at your word I will let down the nets
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that Simon acts because Jesus told him to.

decisions.choice: Maestro
decisions.reason: Luke's word is one who is in charge and gives orders (meaning decision m1). Spanish "maestro" also means a master in charge of a work, and is the respectful address Spanish readers expect; "jefe" and "patrón" sound like an employer, and "Señor" is kept for "Lord". The cost is that it is the same word as "Teacher" elsewhere.

decisions.choice: Mkuu
decisions.reason: Luke's word is one who is in charge and gives orders (meaning decision m1). "Mkuu" (chief, superior) is how a worker respectfully addresses the one over him. "Mwalimu" is kept for "Teacher" and "Bwana" for "Lord", so Luke's three titles stay distinct.

source.text: καὶ τοῦτο ποιήσαντες συνέκλεισαν πλῆθος ἰχθύων πολύ, διερρήσσετο δὲ τὰ δίκτυα αὐτῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And this having done they enclosed a multitude of fish great, were being torn and the nets of them.

en.L: And when they had done this, they enclosed a great number of fish, and their nets were beginning to tear.
en.B: So they did this, and they closed their nets around a great mass of fish. Their nets were starting to tear.
en.R: They did what Jesus said. They caught so many fish that the nets started tearing apart.

es.L: Y habiendo hecho esto, encerraron una gran cantidad de peces, y sus redes comenzaban a romperse.
es.B: Así lo hicieron, y atraparon en las redes una enorme cantidad de peces. Las redes empezaban a romperse.
es.R: Hicieron lo que Jesús les dijo. Atraparon tantos peces que las redes empezaron a romperse.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kufanya hivyo, walifungia samaki wengi mno, na nyavu zao zikaanza kuchanika.
sw.B: Basi walifanya hivyo, wakazungushia nyavu kundi kubwa la samaki. Nyavu zao zikaanza kuchanika.
sw.R: Walifanya kama Yesu alivyosema. Wakavua samaki wengi sana hata nyavu zikaanza kuchanika.

decisions.choice: were breaking: the nets began to tear
alternatives: the nets broke and the fish were lost
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes what was starting to happen. The catch was saved (5:7, 9).

decisions.choice: what Jesus said
decisions.reason: Readable says what they had done.

source.text: καὶ κατένευσαν τοῖς μετόχοις ἐν τῷ ἑτέρῳ πλοίῳ τοῦ ἐλθόντας συλλαβέσθαι αὐτοῖς· καὶ ἦλθον, καὶ ἔπλησαν ἀμφότερα τὰ πλοῖα ὥστε βυθίζεσθαι αὐτά.

records.literal_gloss: And they signaled to the partners in the other boat, the having come to help them; and they came, and filled both the boats so that were sinking them.

en.L: And they signaled to [their] partners in the other boat to come [and] help them; and they came and filled both boats, so that they were beginning to sink.
en.B: They waved to their partners in the other boat to come over and lend a hand. The partners came, and together they loaded both boats with fish until the boats were starting to go under.
en.R: So they waved to the men in the other boat, who worked with them, to come and help. The men came. They put so many fish into both boats that the boats were about to sink.

es.L: Y hicieron señas a [sus] compañeros de la otra barca para que vinieran a ayudarlos; y vinieron y llenaron ambas barcas, de modo que comenzaban a hundirse.
es.B: Hicieron señas a sus compañeros de la otra barca para que vinieran a echarles una mano. Ellos vinieron, y entre todos llenaron de peces las dos barcas, hasta el punto de que empezaban a hundirse.
es.R: Entonces hicieron señas a los hombres de la otra barca, que trabajaban con ellos, para que vinieran a ayudar. Ellos vinieron. Echaron tantos peces en las dos barcas que casi se hundían.

sw.L: Nao wakawaashiria wenzao katika mashua ile nyingine waje kuwasaidia; nao wakaja, wakajaza mashua zote mbili, hata zikaanza kuzama.
sw.B: Waliwapungia mikono wenzao waliokuwa katika mashua nyingine ili waje kuwasaidia. Nao wakaja, wakazijaza samaki mashua zote mbili hata zikaanza kuzama.
sw.R: Basi waliwapungia mikono watu waliokuwa katika mashua nyingine, ambao walifanya kazi pamoja nao, ili waje kuwasaidia. Watu hao wakaja. Wakajaza samaki wengi katika mashua zote mbili hata zikakaribia kuzama.

decisions.choice: partners: fellow fishermen who worked with Simon
decisions.reason: Luke names them in 5:10: James and John, Zebedee's sons, who were partners with Simon.

decisions.choice: were sinking: were beginning to sink
decisions.reason: The verb describes what was about to happen; the boats reached land (5:11).

decisions.choice: the men in the other boat, who worked with them
decisions.reason: Readable explains the word.

source.text: ἰδὼν δὲ Σίμων Πέτρος προσέπεσεν τοῖς γόνασιν Ἰησοῦ λέγων· Ἔξελθε ἀπ’ ἐμοῦ, ὅτι ἀνὴρ ἁμαρτωλός εἰμι, κύριε·

records.literal_gloss: Having seen and Simon Peter fell at the knees of Jesus saying, Depart from me, for a man sinful I am, Lord.

en.L: And when Simon Peter saw [it], he fell down at the knees of Jesus, saying, "Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, Lord."
en.B: When Simon Peter saw this, he threw himself down at Jesus's knees and said, "Lord, leave me! I am a man full of sin."
en.R: When Simon Peter saw this, he knelt down in front of Jesus. He said, "Lord, go away from me! I am a sinner, and I am not fit to be near {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

es.L: Y al ver[lo], Simón Pedro cayó a las rodillas de Jesús, diciendo: «Aléjate de mí, porque soy un hombre pecador, Señor».
es.B: Cuando Simón Pedro vio esto, se dejó caer de rodillas ante Jesús y dijo: «¡Señor, aléjate de mí! Soy un hombre lleno de pecado».
es.R: Cuando Simón Pedro vio esto, se arrodilló delante de Jesús. Le dijo: «¡Señor, vete lejos de mí! Soy un pecador, y no merezco estar cerca de {{deity_pronoun:ti|Ti}}».

sw.L: Simoni Petro alipoona [hivyo], alianguka magotini pa Yesu, akisema, "Nenda mbali nami, kwa sababu mimi ni mtu mwenye dhambi, Bwana."
sw.B: Simoni Petro alipoona hayo, alijitupa chini magotini pa Yesu, akasema, "Bwana, niache! Mimi ni mtu aliyejaa dhambi."
sw.R: Simoni Petro alipoona hayo, alipiga magoti mbele ya Yesu. Akasema, "Bwana, ondoka mbali nami! Mimi ni mwenye dhambi, wala sistahili kuwa karibu {{deity_pronoun:nawe|Nawe}}."

decisions.choice: Peter: the name Jesus gives Simon
decisions.reason: Luke tells in 6:14 that Jesus named Simon "Peter", which means rock. Here, at the moment Simon is called, Luke uses both names.

decisions.choice: Lord: more than a polite title here
decisions.reason: The same word can be a polite "sir". Simon called Jesus "Master" (5:5); now, on his knees and confessing his sin, he uses the word Luke uses for God and for Jesus (2:11).

decisions.choice: depart from me, for I am a sinful man: the fear of a sinful person before God's holiness
alternatives: embarrassment at his failure as a fisherman
decisions.reason: When Isaiah saw the Lord, he cried out that he was lost, a man of unclean lips (Isaiah 6:5). Simon sees God's power at work in Jesus and feels unworthy to be near him.

decisions.choice: I am not fit to be near you
decisions.reason: Readable spells out why Simon asks Jesus to leave, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: Señor, with a capital
decisions.reason: Here the word is more than a polite title (meaning decision m2): Simon speaks as a sinner before God's holiness. So it is "Señor", the word for the Lord, not lowercase "señor" (sir).

decisions.choice: Bwana, with a capital
decisions.reason: Here the word is more than polite address (meaning decision m2): Simon speaks as a sinner before God's holiness. So it is "Bwana", as for the Lord, not lowercase "bwana" (sir).

source.text: θάμβος γὰρ περιέσχεν αὐτὸν καὶ πάντας τοὺς σὺν αὐτῷ ἐπὶ τῇ ἄγρᾳ τῶν ἰχθύων ὧν συνέλαβον, ὁμοίως δὲ καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην υἱοὺς Ζεβεδαίου, οἳ ἦσαν κοινωνοὶ τῷ Σίμωνι.

records.literal_gloss: Amazement for seized him and all the [ones] with him at the catch of the fish which they took, \v 10 likewise and also James and John sons of Zebedee, who were partners with the Simon.

en.L: For amazement had seized him and all those with him at the catch of fish that they had taken, \v 10 and likewise also James and John, sons of Zebedee, who were partners with Simon.
en.B: He said this because the haul of fish they had brought in had left him stunned, and all who were with him as well. \v 10 Zebedee's sons, James and John, Simon's partners, were stunned in the same way.
en.R: Simon and all the men with him were amazed at how many fish they had caught. \v 10 James and John, the sons of Zebedee, were amazed too. They were Simon's partners in the fishing business.

es.L: Porque el asombro se había apoderado de él y de todos los que [estaban] con él por la pesca de peces que habían sacado, \v 10 e igualmente también de Santiago y de Juan, hijos de Zebedeo, que eran socios de Simón.
es.B: Dijo esto porque la pesca que habían sacado lo había dejado atónito, a él y a todos los que lo acompañaban. \v 10 Lo mismo les pasó a Santiago y a Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, que eran socios de Simón.
es.R: Simón y todos los que estaban con él quedaron asombrados de ver cuántos peces habían pescado. \v 10 Santiago y Juan, los hijos de Zebedeo, también quedaron asombrados. Ellos eran socios de Simón en el negocio de la pesca.

sw.L: Kwa maana mshangao ulimshika yeye na wote waliokuwa pamoja naye kwa sababu ya samaki waliowavua, \v 10 na vivyo hivyo pia Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, waliokuwa washirika wa Simoni.
sw.B: Alisema hivyo kwa sababu yeye na wote waliokuwa pamoja naye walishangaa mno kwa wingi wa samaki waliowavua. \v 10 Wana wa Zebedayo, Yakobo na Yohana, washirika wa Simoni, nao walishangaa vivyo hivyo.
sw.R: Simoni na watu wote waliokuwa pamoja naye walishangaa sana kuona samaki wengi kiasi kile. \v 10 Yakobo na Yohana, wana wa Zebedayo, nao walishangaa pia. Wao walikuwa washirika wa Simoni katika biashara ya uvuvi.

decisions.choice: for: this explains Simon's words in 5:8
decisions.reason: Simon spoke as he did because the catch had overwhelmed him.

decisions.choice: amazement: astonishment mixed with fear
decisions.reason: The word is used of people faced with a power they cannot explain (4:36; Acts 3:10).

decisions.choice: partners: sharers in a business
decisions.reason: The word means people who share something, here a fishing business.

decisions.choice: He said this because
decisions.reason: Balanced makes the connection with 5:8 plain.

decisions.choice: partners in the fishing business
decisions.reason: Readable says what they were partners in.

source.text: καὶ εἶπεν πρὸς τὸν Σίμωνα ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Μὴ φοβοῦ· ἀπὸ τοῦ νῦν ἀνθρώπους ἔσῃ ζωγρῶν.

records.literal_gloss: And said to the Simon the Jesus, Not fear; from the now people you will be catching alive.

en.L: And Jesus said to Simon, "Do not be afraid; from now on you will be catching {{gender:people|men}} alive."
en.B: "Do not be afraid," Jesus told Simon. "From now on you will be catching {{gender:people|men}}."
en.R: "Do not be afraid," Jesus said to Simon. "From now on you will catch {{gender:people|men}} instead of fish."

es.L: Y Jesús dijo a Simón: «No temas; desde ahora estarás atrapando con vida a {{gender:personas|hombres}}».
es.B: «No tengas miedo», le dijo Jesús a Simón. «Desde ahora vas a pescar {{gender:personas|hombres}}».
es.R: «No tengas miedo», le dijo Jesús a Simón. «Desde ahora pescarás {{gender:personas|hombres}} en vez de peces».

sw.L: Na Yesu akamwambia Simoni, "Usiogope; tangu sasa utakuwa ukiwavua watu wakiwa hai."
sw.B: "Usiogope," Yesu alimwambia Simoni. "Tangu sasa utakuwa ukivua watu."
sw.R: "Usiogope," Yesu alimwambia Simoni. "Tangu sasa utavua watu badala ya samaki."

decisions.choice: catching alive: taking people alive, to save them
decisions.reason: The verb means to take alive, as soldiers took prisoners alive. Fish that are caught die; the people Simon catches will live. Simon's work will be to gather people for God.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The noun is the general word for human beings.

decisions.choice: you will be catching: an ongoing work
decisions.reason: "Will be" with the participle describes a lasting task from now on.

decisions.choice: do not be afraid: Simon need not fear being near Jesus
alternatives: do not fear the storm or the sea
decisions.reason: Jesus answers Simon's fear in 5:8, as angels answered Zechariah and Mary (1:13, 30).

decisions.choice: instead of fish
decisions.reason: Readable makes the comparison with Simon's work plain. It does not try to bring out "alive", which the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: atrapando con vida
decisions.reason: The Greek verb means to catch alive, to take a captive and keep him living (meaning decision m1). Literal says so; Balanced and Readable say "pescar", as the English does.

decisions.choice: watu, with no gender span
decisions.reason: The English sets "people" against "men" under the gender setting. "Watu" already means people, men and women (meaning decision m2); "wanaume" would mean males only and change the meaning, so Swahili has no span here, as in Matthew 4:19.

source.text: καὶ καταγαγόντες τὰ πλοῖα ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν ἀφέντες πάντα ἠκολούθησαν αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having brought the boats onto the land, having left all they followed him.

en.L: And when they had brought the boats to land, they left everything and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Once the boats were on land, they walked away from everything and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: They brought their boats to the shore. Then they left everything behind and followed Jesus.

es.L: Y habiendo llevado las barcas a tierra, dejándolo todo, {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.B: Una vez que sacaron las barcas a tierra, lo dejaron todo y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguieron.
es.R: Llevaron sus barcas a la orilla. Luego dejaron todo atrás y siguieron a Jesús.

sw.L: Na walipokwisha kuzileta mashua nchi kavu, wakaacha vyote, wakamfuata.
sw.B: Walipozifikisha mashua ufuoni, waliacha kila kitu, wakamfuata.
sw.R: Walizileta mashua zao ufuoni. Kisha wakaacha kila kitu, wakamfuata Yesu.

decisions.choice: followed: went with him as his disciples
alternatives: walked behind him for a time
decisions.reason: To follow Jesus is to become his disciple and share his life (5:27-28; 9:23).

decisions.choice: everything: their boats, their trade, and even the great catch
decisions.reason: They leave behind the very catch they had just made. Levi will do the same (5:28; 18:28).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ εἶναι αὐτὸν ἐν μιᾷ τῶν πόλεων καὶ ἰδοὺ ἀνὴρ πλήρης λέπρας· καὶ ἰδὼν τὸν Ἰησοῦν πεσὼν ἐπὶ πρόσωπον ἐδεήθη αὐτοῦ λέγων· Κύριε, ἐὰν θέλῃς δύνασαί με καθαρίσαι.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass in the being him in one of the cities and look a man full of leprosy; having seen and the Jesus, having fallen on face he begged him saying, Lord, if you are willing, you are able me to cleanse.

en.L: And it happened, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in one of the towns, that look, [there was] a man full of leprosy; and when he saw Jesus, he fell on [his] face and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are willing, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are able to make me clean."
en.B: In one of the towns where Jesus was, there was a man covered all over with leprosy. Seeing Jesus, he fell face down and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can make me clean, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} choose to."
en.R: Jesus was in one of the towns. A man there had a terrible skin disease all over his body. When the man saw Jesus, he bowed down with his face to the ground. He begged Jesus, "Lord, if {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} want to, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can heal me and make me clean."

es.L: Y sucedió que, estando {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} en uno de los pueblos, mira, [había] un hombre lleno de lepra; y al ver a Jesús, cayendo sobre [su] rostro, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} rogó, diciendo: «Señor, si quieres, puedes limpiarme».
es.B: En uno de los pueblos donde estaba Jesús, había un hombre cubierto de lepra. Al ver a Jesús, se postró rostro en tierra y {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suplicó: «Señor, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}} puedes dejarme limpio, si quieres».
es.R: Jesús estaba en uno de los pueblos. Allí había un hombre que tenía una grave enfermedad de la piel por todo el cuerpo. Cuando el hombre vio a Jesús, se inclinó hasta tocar el suelo con la cara. Le rogó a Jesús: «Señor, si quieres, puedes sanarme y dejarme limpio».

sw.L: Na ikawa alipokuwa katika mojawapo ya miji, tazama, [palikuwa na] mtu aliyejaa ukoma; naye alipomwona Yesu, akianguka kifudifudi, alimsihi, akisema, "Bwana, ukitaka, unaweza kunitakasa."
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa katika mji mmoja, palikuwa na mtu aliyekuwa na ukoma mwili mzima. Alipomwona Yesu, alianguka kifudifudi, akamsihi, "Bwana, {{deity_pronoun:wewe|Wewe}} unaweza kunifanya safi, ukipenda."
sw.R: Yesu alikuwa katika mji mmoja. Huko kulikuwa na mtu mwenye ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi mwili mzima. Mtu huyo alipomwona Yesu, aliinama mpaka uso wake ukagusa ardhi. Akamsihi Yesu, "Bwana, ukitaka, unaweza kuniponya na kunifanya safi."

decisions.choice: leprosy: a serious skin disease that made a person unclean under the law
alternatives: only the disease now called leprosy (Hansen's disease)
decisions.reason: The law of Moses gives the word to several kinds of skin disease, and even to mold in clothing and houses (Leviticus 13-14). A priest examined the skin and declared the person clean or unclean. Someone with the disease had to tear his clothes, cry "Unclean!" and live outside the camp, apart from others (Leviticus 13:45-46), and could not take part in worship.

decisions.choice: full of leprosy: the disease covered his body
decisions.reason: "Full of" means the disease had spread over much of his body. Luke, the doctor (Colossians 4:14), alone notes it.

decisions.choice: make clean: heal, so that he can be declared clean
decisions.reason: The law speaks of "cleansing" from this disease (Leviticus 14:2). A priest could declare a person clean once the disease had gone, but could not make it go. The man asks Jesus to do what the law could not.

decisions.choice: if you are willing, you can: the man does not doubt Jesus's power, only whether he wants to use it for him
decisions.reason: The question is not whether Jesus can, but whether he will.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: a terrible skin disease; heal me and make me clean
decisions.reason: Readable describes the disease instead of naming it, because "leprosy" now means one particular disease. It also says that being clean meant being healed.

decisions.choice: you can make me clean, if you choose to
alternatives: if you are willing, you can make me clean
decisions.reason: Balanced puts the man's confidence first and his request second.

decisions.choice: lleno de lepra (L); cubierto de lepra (B); una grave enfermedad de la piel por todo el cuerpo (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 8:2: the Greek word covers several skin diseases that made a person unclean (meaning decision m1). Readable describes it rather than naming modern leprosy, as the English Readable does. The same in verse 13.

decisions.choice: aliyejaa ukoma (L); mwenye ukoma mwili mzima (B); mwenye ugonjwa mbaya wa ngozi (R)
decisions.reason: As in Matthew 8:2: the Greek word covers several skin diseases that made a person unclean (meaning decision m1). Readable describes it rather than naming modern leprosy, as the English Readable does. The same in verse 13.

source.text: καὶ ἐκτείνας τὴν χεῖρα ἥψατο αὐτοῦ εἰπών· Θέλω, καθαρίσθητι· καὶ εὐθέως ἡ λέπρα ἀπῆλθεν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having stretched out the hand he touched him saying, I am willing, be cleansed; and immediately the leprosy departed from him.

en.L: And stretching out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched him, saying, "I am willing; be cleansed." And immediately the leprosy departed from him.
en.B: He stretched out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and laid it on the man. "I do want to," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said. "Be made clean." The leprosy left him that very moment.
en.R: Jesus put out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand and touched the man. "I do want to," Jesus said. "Be healed and clean!" Right away the man's skin disease was gone.

es.L: Y extendiendo la mano, lo tocó, diciendo: «Quiero; sé limpiado». Y al instante la lepra se fue de él.
es.B: Extendió la mano y tocó al hombre. «Sí quiero», le dijo. «Queda limpio». En ese mismo momento la lepra lo dejó.
es.R: Jesús extendió la mano y tocó al hombre. «Sí quiero», le dijo Jesús. «¡Queda sano y limpio!». Enseguida la enfermedad de la piel desapareció.

sw.L: Naye akinyoosha mkono, alimgusa, akisema, "Nataka; takasika." Na mara ukoma ukamtoka.
sw.B: Alinyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamgusa yule mtu. "Ndiyo, nataka," akasema. "Uwe safi." Saa ile ile ukoma ukamwacha.
sw.R: Yesu alinyoosha mkono {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, akamgusa yule mtu. "Nataka," Yesu akasema. "Pona, uwe safi!" Mara moja ugonjwa wa ngozi wa yule mtu ukatoweka.

decisions.choice: he touched him: touching an unclean person made a person unclean
alternatives: a touch with no special meaning
decisions.reason: The law treated contact with an unclean person as making a person unclean (Leviticus 5:3). Jesus is not made unclean; instead the man is made clean.

decisions.choice: be cleansed: a command that takes effect at once
decisions.reason: The passive command answers the man's request word for word, and Luke says the disease left at once.

decisions.choice: I am willing: the answer to "if you are willing"
decisions.reason: Jesus takes up the man's own verb from 5:12.

decisions.choice: the man (B, R); him (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable make clear whom Jesus touched.

decisions.choice: la mano, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English marks "his hand". The Greek says "the hand", and Spanish uses the article for one's own body, so there is no possessive to capitalise.

source.text: καὶ αὐτὸς παρήγγειλεν αὐτῷ μηδενὶ εἰπεῖν, ἀλλὰ ἀπελθὼν δεῖξον σεαυτὸν τῷ ἱερεῖ, καὶ προσένεγκε περὶ τοῦ καθαρισμοῦ σου καθὼς προσέταξεν Μωϋσῆς εἰς μαρτύριον αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And he ordered him no one to tell, but having gone show yourself to the priest and offer for the cleansing of you as commanded Moses, for a testimony to them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered him to tell no one, "But go, show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them."
en.B: Jesus gave him strict orders not to tell anyone. "Instead," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "go and let the priest examine you. Then bring the offering Moses ordered for your cleansing, as evidence to them."
en.R: Jesus told him, "Do not tell anyone about this. Instead, go to the priest and let him look at your skin. Then give the offering that Moses commanded for people who have been made clean. This will show everyone that you are healed."

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} le ordenó que no se lo dijera a nadie: «Sino ve, muéstrate al sacerdote y haz una ofrenda por tu purificación, como mandó Moisés, como testimonio para ellos».
es.B: Jesús le ordenó con firmeza que no se lo contara a nadie. «Más bien», le dijo, «ve y deja que el sacerdote te examine. Después lleva la ofrenda que mandó Moisés por tu purificación, como prueba para ellos».
es.R: Jesús le dijo: «No le cuentes esto a nadie. Más bien, ve al sacerdote y deja que te revise la piel. Después presenta la ofrenda que mandó Moisés para los que han quedado limpios. Así todos sabrán que estás sano».

sw.L: Naye akamwagiza asimwambie mtu yeyote, "Lakini nenda, ujionyeshe kwa kuhani, utoe [sadaka] kwa ajili ya kutakaswa kwako, kama Musa alivyoamuru, kuwa ushuhuda kwao."
sw.B: Yesu alimwagiza kwa nguvu asimwambie mtu yeyote. "Badala yake," akasema, "nenda kwa kuhani akuchunguze. Kisha utoe sadaka ambayo Musa aliamuru kwa ajili ya kutakaswa kwako, iwe uthibitisho kwao."
sw.R: Yesu alimwambia, "Usimwambie mtu yeyote habari hii. Badala yake, nenda kwa kuhani akuangalie ngozi yako. Kisha utoe sadaka ambayo Musa aliamuru kwa watu waliofanywa safi. Hiyo itawaonyesha watu wote kwamba umepona."

decisions.choice: show yourself to the priest and offer: the steps the law of Moses set out for a person cleansed of the disease
alternatives: a new rule given by Jesus
decisions.reason: Leviticus 14:1-32 tells how a priest examined the person outside the camp, and how, after washing and offerings of birds and lambs (or doves for the poor), the person was declared clean and could return to the community and its worship.

decisions.choice: the order begins as reported speech and turns into Jesus's own words
decisions.reason: Luke moves from "he ordered him to tell no one" straight into the words Jesus spoke, "but go, show yourself". He does the same in Acts 1:4.

decisions.choice: as a testimony to them: as evidence to the priests and the people that the man is clean
decisions.reason: The priest's declaration would let everyone know the man was clean again, and so would show what God had done. Some take "them" as the priests and the testimony as a challenge to them.

decisions.choice: the order to tell no one also as Jesus's own words (R); reported, then quoted (L, B)
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the shift into direct speech; Readable puts all of the order in Jesus's words, which is easier to follow.

decisions.choice: This will show everyone that you are healed
decisions.reason: Readable gives the more likely sense, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: utoe [sadaka]
decisions.reason: The Greek "offer for your cleansing" leaves the offering unnamed. A Swahili verb of giving needs an object, so Literal supplies it in brackets; the English Literal can say "make an offering" without one.

source.text: διήρχετο δὲ μᾶλλον ὁ λόγος περὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ συνήρχοντο ὄχλοι πολλοὶ ἀκούειν καὶ θεραπεύεσθαι ἀπὸ τῶν ἀσθενειῶν αὐτῶν·

records.literal_gloss: Was spreading and still more the word about him, and were coming together crowds many to hear and to be healed from the sicknesses of them;

en.L: But the word about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was spreading still more, and many crowds were coming together to hear and to be healed of their sicknesses.
en.B: But word about Jesus went out farther than ever. Large crowds kept gathering to listen and to be healed of their illnesses.
en.R: But the news about Jesus kept spreading even more. Big crowds came to hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} teach, and to have {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} heal their sicknesses.

es.L: Pero la noticia acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se extendía todavía más, y se reunían muchas multitudes para oír y ser sanadas de sus enfermedades.
es.B: Pero lo que se decía de Jesús se extendía más que nunca. Grandes multitudes seguían reuniéndose para escuchar y para ser sanadas de sus enfermedades.
es.R: Pero la noticia sobre Jesús seguía corriendo cada vez más. Llegaban muchísimas personas para oír lo que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} enseñaba y para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} las sanara de sus enfermedades.

sw.L: Lakini habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} zilizidi kuenea, na makundi mengi ya watu yakawa yakikusanyika kusikia na kuponywa magonjwa yao.
sw.B: Lakini habari za Yesu zilienea kuliko wakati wowote. Makundi makubwa ya watu yaliendelea kukusanyika ili kusikiliza na kuponywa magonjwa yao.
sw.R: Lakini habari za Yesu ziliendelea kuenea zaidi na zaidi. Makundi makubwa ya watu yalikuja kumsikiliza akifundisha, na ili awaponye magonjwa yao.

decisions.choice: the word about him: the report, the news
decisions.reason: The noun means a spoken account; here what people were saying about Jesus (7:17).

decisions.choice: but still more: in spite of the order to tell no one, the news spread even more
decisions.reason: Luke does not say who spread it; he says the order did not stop it.

decisions.choice: Jesus (B, R); him (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: to hear him teach, and to have him heal
alternatives: to hear and to be healed
decisions.reason: Readable says whom they came to hear and who healed them.

source.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ἦν ὑποχωρῶν ἐν ταῖς ἐρήμοις καὶ προσευχόμενος.

records.literal_gloss: He himself but was withdrawing in the wilderness [places] and praying.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} would withdraw into the wilderness [places] and pray.
en.B: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} kept slipping away to places in the wilderness to pray.
en.R: But Jesus would often go away to places where no one lived, so {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could pray.

es.L: Pero {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} solía retirarse a los [lugares] desiertos y orar.
es.B: Sin embargo, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se apartaba una y otra vez a lugares desiertos para orar.
es.R: Pero Jesús a menudo se iba a lugares donde no vivía nadie, para poder orar.

sw.L: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}} alikuwa akijitenga mahali pa nyika na kuomba.
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akijiondoa mara kwa mara, akaenda mahali pa nyika ili kuomba.
sw.R: Lakini Yesu mara nyingi alikwenda mahali pasipo na watu, ili apate kuomba.

decisions.choice: was withdrawing and praying: his habit
decisions.reason: "Was" with the participles describes something Jesus did again and again. Prayer marks the turning points of Jesus's life in Luke (3:21; 6:12; 9:18).

decisions.choice: the wilderness places: lonely places away from towns
decisions.reason: The word is plural: deserted places, as in 4:42.

decisions.choice: he himself, but: in contrast to the crowds seeking him
decisions.reason: Luke sets Jesus's withdrawal against the crowds who came to him (5:15).

decisions.choice: kept slipping away (B); would often go away (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable bring out the habit, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: one span, on él
alternatives: él mismo with a second span
decisions.reason: The English marks both "he" and "himself". Spanish shows the emphasis of the Greek pronoun (meaning decision m3) with a stated "él"; adding "mismo" would sound forced.

decisions.choice: mahali pa nyika (L, B); mahali pasipo na watu (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: "nyika" is open, empty country, which is what is meant (meaning decision m2); "jangwa" suggests sand desert. Readable says what the places were, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν μιᾷ τῶν ἡμερῶν καὶ αὐτὸς ἦν διδάσκων, καὶ ἦσαν καθήμενοι Φαρισαῖοι καὶ νομοδιδάσκαλοι οἳ ἦσαν ἐληλυθότες ἐκ πάσης κώμης τῆς Γαλιλαίας καὶ Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλήμ· καὶ δύναμις κυρίου ἦν εἰς τὸ ἰᾶσθαι αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: And it came to pass on one of the days and he was teaching, and were sitting Pharisees and teachers of the law who were having come out of every village of the Galilee and Judea and Jerusalem; and power of Lord was for the to heal him.

en.L: And it happened on one of the days that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, and Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting [there], who had come out of every village of Galilee and Judea and [from] Jerusalem; and [the] power of [the] Lord was [there] for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to heal.
en.B: On one of those days, while {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching, some Pharisees and teachers of the law were seated there. They had come from all the villages of Galilee, from Judea, and from Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was present for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to heal.
en.R: One day Jesus was teaching. Some Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every town in Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. The Lord God was giving Jesus power to heal people.

es.L: Y sucedió en uno de los días que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba enseñando, y estaban sentados [allí] fariseos y maestros de la ley que habían venido de todas las aldeas de Galilea y de Judea y [de] Jerusalén; y [el] poder de[l] Señor estaba [allí] para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sanara.
es.B: Uno de esos días, mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} enseñaba, estaban sentados allí unos fariseos y maestros de la ley. Habían venido de todas las aldeas de Galilea, de Judea y de Jerusalén. El poder del Señor estaba presente para que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} sanara.
es.R: Un día Jesús estaba enseñando. Algunos fariseos y maestros de la ley estaban sentados allí. Habían venido de todos los pueblos de Galilea y de Judea, y también de Jerusalén. El Señor Dios le daba a Jesús poder para sanar a la gente.

sw.L: Na ikawa katika mojawapo ya siku hizo {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} alikuwa akifundisha, na walikuwa wameketi [pale] Mafarisayo na walimu wa sheria, waliokuwa wametoka katika kila kijiji cha Galilaya na Uyahudi na Yerusalemu; na nguvu za Bwana zilikuwa [pale] ili {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} aponye.
sw.B: Siku moja kati ya siku hizo, alipokuwa akifundisha, Mafarisayo na walimu wa sheria walikuwa wameketi pale. Walikuwa wametoka katika vijiji vyote vya Galilaya, na Uyahudi, na Yerusalemu. Nguvu za Bwana zilikuwa pamoja {{deity_pronoun:naye|Naye}} ili aponye.
sw.R: Siku moja Yesu alikuwa akifundisha. Baadhi ya Mafarisayo na walimu wa sheria walikuwa wameketi pale. Walikuwa wametoka katika kila mji wa Galilaya na Uyahudi, na pia Yerusalemu. Bwana Mungu alikuwa akimpa Yesu nguvu ya kuponya watu.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping the law of Moses exactly
decisions.reason: The Pharisees studied the law closely and kept the traditions handed down by earlier teachers on how to obey it, especially about the Sabbath, tithing, fasting and ritual cleanness (Galatians 1:14; Acts 26:5). Paul had been one (Philippians 3:5). Many people respected them. This is their first appearance in Luke.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law: experts who taught and explained the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word is used of Gamaliel, a Pharisee honored by all the people (Acts 5:34). Luke also calls these experts "scribes" (5:21).

decisions.choice: him: the power of the Lord was there for Jesus to heal, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: them: for him to heal them, the reading of many later manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts read "him", as the subject of the healing. Many later manuscripts read "them", the sick he healed. The sense is close. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the power of the Lord: God's power
decisions.reason: "Lord" here is God, as often in Luke 1-2 (1:66; 2:9). Jesus heals by the power of the Spirit (4:14, 18).

decisions.choice: teachers of the law
decisions.reason: This word means teachers of the law, so every level says so. Luke's other word for these experts is rendered "scribes" (L, B) in 5:21.

decisions.choice: The Lord God was giving Jesus power to heal people
alternatives: the power of the Lord was there for him to heal
decisions.reason: Readable says whose power it was and whom Jesus healed.

decisions.choice: maestros de la ley (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke's word means teachers of the law (meaning decision m2), and Spanish says just that at every level. "Doctores de la ley" is the older phrase but now suggests physicians; "escribas" is kept for the scribes of verse 21.

decisions.choice: walimu wa sheria (every level)
decisions.reason: Luke's word means teachers of the law (meaning decision m2), and Swahili says just that at every level. Readable uses the same words for the scribes of verse 21, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄνδρες φέροντες ἐπὶ κλίνης ἄνθρωπον ὃς ἦν παραλελυμένος, καὶ ἐζήτουν αὐτὸν εἰσενεγκεῖν καὶ θεῖναι ἐνώπιον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And look men carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were seeking him to bring in and to place before him.

en.L: And look, men [were] carrying on a bed a man who was paralyzed, and they were trying to bring him in and to lay [him] before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Just then some men arrived with a paralyzed man lying on a bed. They wanted to carry him in and lay him in front of Jesus.
en.R: Some men brought a man who could not move his body. They carried him on a mat. They wanted to take him into the house and put him down in front of Jesus.

es.L: Y mira, [unos] hombres [venían] llevando sobre una cama a un hombre que estaba paralizado, y buscaban meterlo y poner[lo] delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.
es.B: En ese momento llegaron unos hombres que traían en una camilla a un hombre paralítico. Querían entrar con él y ponerlo delante de Jesús.
es.R: Unos hombres trajeron a un hombre que no podía mover el cuerpo. Lo llevaban en una camilla. Querían meterlo en la casa y ponerlo delante de Jesús.

sw.L: Na tazama, watu wakimbeba juu ya kitanda mtu aliyekuwa amepooza, nao walikuwa wakitafuta [njia ya] kumwingiza na kumweka mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.
sw.B: Mara watu fulani walifika wamembeba juu ya machela mtu aliyepooza. Walitaka kumwingiza ndani na kumweka mbele ya Yesu.
sw.R: Watu fulani walimleta mtu ambaye hakuweza kuusogeza mwili wake. Walimbeba juu ya mkeka. Walitaka kumwingiza ndani ya nyumba na kumweka chini mbele ya Yesu.

decisions.choice: a bed: a light pallet or mat that could be carried
decisions.reason: The word is a general word for a bed. Luke calls it a little bed in 5:19 and 24: something light enough for men to carry.

decisions.choice: paralyzed: unable to move his limbs
decisions.reason: The man had to be carried; he could not walk (5:23-25).

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: into the house
decisions.reason: Readable says where they wanted to bring him; the roof in 5:19 shows it was a house.

decisions.choice: a mat
decisions.reason: Readable uses the word for something light that could be carried.

decisions.choice: cama (L); camilla (B, R)
decisions.reason: A light bed or pallet that could be carried (meaning decision m1). Literal keeps "bed"; Balanced and Readable say "camilla", the carrying bed, as Mark 2:4 does. In verse 19 Luke's diminutive is "camilla" at every level.

decisions.choice: kitanda (L); machela (B); mkeka (R)
decisions.reason: A light bed or pallet that could be carried (meaning decision m1), as in Matthew 9:2: Literal keeps "bed", Balanced says "machela" (stretcher), Readable "mkeka" (mat), as the English Readable does. The same in verses 19 and 24.

source.text: καὶ μὴ εὑρόντες ποίας εἰσενέγκωσιν αὐτὸν διὰ τὸν ὄχλον ἀναβάντες ἐπὶ τὸ δῶμα διὰ τῶν κεράμων καθῆκαν αὐτὸν σὺν τῷ κλινιδίῳ εἰς τὸ μέσον ἔμπροσθεν τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And not having found by what [way] they might bring in him because of the crowd, having gone up on the roof through the tiles they let down him with the little bed into the middle in front of the Jesus.

en.L: And not finding by what [way] they might bring him in because of the crowd, they went up on the roof and let him down through the tiles with [his] little bed into the middle, in front of Jesus.
en.B: The crowd left them no way of getting him in. So they climbed up on the roof, took away some of the tiles, and let him down on his bed into the middle of everyone, in front of Jesus.
en.R: But there were too many people, and the men could not get him through the crowd. So they went up onto the flat roof of the house. They removed some of the tiles and made a hole. Then they let the man down on his mat into the middle of the people, right in front of Jesus.

es.L: Y no hallando por dónde meterlo a causa de la multitud, subiendo a la azotea, lo bajaron por entre las tejas con la camilla al medio, delante de Jesús.
es.B: Como la multitud no les dejaba ninguna manera de entrar con él, subieron a la azotea, quitaron algunas tejas y lo bajaron en la camilla hasta el centro de todos, delante de Jesús.
es.R: Pero había demasiada gente, y los hombres no podían pasar con él entre la multitud. Así que subieron al techo plano de la casa. Quitaron algunas tejas e hicieron un hueco. Después bajaron al hombre en su camilla hasta el medio de la gente, justo delante de Jesús.

sw.L: Na wasipoona [njia] ya kumwingiza kwa sababu ya umati, walipanda juu ya paa, wakamshusha kupitia vigae pamoja na kitanda [chake] kidogo hadi katikati, mbele ya Yesu.
sw.B: Umati haukuwaachia njia yoyote ya kumwingiza. Basi walipanda juu ya paa, wakaondoa baadhi ya vigae, wakamshusha pamoja na machela yake mpaka katikati ya watu wote, mbele ya Yesu.
sw.R: Lakini watu walikuwa wengi mno, na wale watu hawakuweza kumpitisha katikati ya umati. Basi walipanda juu ya paa la nyumba lililokuwa tambarare. Wakaondoa baadhi ya vigae, wakatoboa tundu. Kisha wakamshusha yule mtu akiwa juu ya mkeka wake mpaka katikati ya watu, mbele kabisa ya Yesu.

decisions.choice: the roof, the tiles: a flat roof that could be opened
decisions.reason: Houses in the land of Israel had flat roofs, often reached by an outside stair, where people could walk (Deuteronomy 22:8; Acts 10:9). Mark says the men dug through the roof (Mark 2:4); Luke speaks of tiles.

decisions.choice: the little bed: the same pallet as in 5:18
decisions.reason: Luke uses a smaller form of the word for the same light bed.

decisions.choice: took away (B) or removed (R) some of the tiles
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say how they made a way through.

decisions.choice: the flat roof of the house
decisions.reason: Readable explains how men could climb onto a roof.

decisions.choice: la azotea (L, B); el techo plano de la casa (R)
decisions.reason: The roof was flat and could be walked on and opened (meaning decision m1). Spanish "azotea" is exactly such a roof; Readable spells it out, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν τὴν πίστιν αὐτῶν εἶπεν· Ἄνθρωπε, ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen the faith of them he said, Man, have been forgiven to you the sins of you.

en.L: And seeing their faith, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Man, your sins have been forgiven you."
en.B: Jesus saw their faith and said, "My friend, your sins stand forgiven."
en.R: Jesus saw that they had faith. He said to the man, "My friend, God has forgiven your sins."

es.L: Y viendo la fe de ellos, dijo: «Hombre, te han sido perdonados tus pecados».
es.B: Jesús vio la fe de ellos y dijo: «Amigo, tus pecados quedan perdonados».
es.R: Jesús vio que tenían fe. Le dijo al hombre: «Amigo, Dios ha perdonado tus pecados».

sw.L: Naye alipoiona imani yao, alisema, "Ewe mtu, zimesamehewa kwako dhambi zako."
sw.B: Yesu alipoona imani yao, alisema, "Rafiki yangu, dhambi zako zimesamehewa."
sw.R: Yesu aliona kwamba walikuwa na imani. Akamwambia yule mtu, "Rafiki yangu, Mungu amekusamehe dhambi zako."

decisions.choice: their faith: the trust of the men who brought him, and probably of the man himself, shown in what they did
alternatives: the faith of the paralyzed man alone
decisions.reason: Their effort to reach Jesus showed that they trusted him to help. In Luke faith is often seen in action (7:9, 50; 8:48).

decisions.choice: have been forgiven: forgiven, and that stands; God is the one who forgives
decisions.reason: The perfect tense describes a forgiveness that holds. The passive leaves God as the one who forgives, which is why the scribes object (5:21).

decisions.choice: Man: a plain, kind way to address someone
decisions.reason: Calling someone "man" was neither rude nor cold (12:14; 22:58).

decisions.choice: My friend
decisions.reason: In modern English "Man" as an address sounds rough. Balanced and Readable give the friendly tone.

decisions.choice: God has forgiven
decisions.reason: Readable names God as the one who forgives, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: καὶ ἤρξαντο διαλογίζεσθαι οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι λέγοντες· Τίς ἐστιν οὗτος ὃς λαλεῖ βλασφημίας;

records.literal_gloss: And began to reason the scribes and the Pharisees saying, Who is this who speaks blasphemies?

en.L: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to reason, saying, "Who is this who speaks blasphemies?
en.B: The scribes and Pharisees started to debate among themselves: "Who is this man, speaking blasphemy like this?
en.R: The teachers of the law and the Pharisees began to ask themselves, "Who is this man? His words are an insult to God!

es.L: Y comenzaron a razonar los escribas y los fariseos, diciendo: «¿Quién es este que habla blasfemias?
es.B: Los escribas y los fariseos se pusieron a discutir entre ellos: «¿Quién es este hombre, que dice tales blasfemias?
es.R: Los maestros de la ley y los fariseos comenzaron a preguntarse: «¿Quién es este hombre? ¡Sus palabras son un insulto contra Dios!

sw.L: Na waandishi na Mafarisayo walianza kuhojiana, wakisema, "Huyu ni nani anayesema makufuru?
sw.B: Waandishi na Mafarisayo walianza kujadiliana wao kwa wao: "Mtu huyu ni nani, anayesema makufuru namna hii?
sw.R: Walimu wa sheria na Mafarisayo walianza kujiuliza, "Mtu huyu ni nani? Maneno yake ni matusi kwa Mungu!

decisions.choice: scribes: experts in the law of Moses
decisions.reason: The word first meant a writer or clerk. In the Gospels it means the experts who copied, studied and taught the law, the same people Luke has just called teachers of the law (5:17).

decisions.choice: blasphemies: words that insult God
decisions.reason: To speak blasphemy was to dishonor God, and the law punished it severely (Leviticus 24:16). They think Jesus has claimed something that belongs to God alone.

decisions.choice: reason: think it over and debate, here in their hearts
decisions.reason: The verb is used of thinking and arguing among people or within oneself. Jesus asks why they reason "in your hearts" (5:22).

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the word "scribes", which today suggests copying, and calls them what they were.

decisions.choice: His words are an insult to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains "blasphemy".

decisions.choice: escribas (L, B); maestros de la ley (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Literal and Balanced keep the title "escribas"; Readable says what these men were, experts in the law (meaning decision m1), as the English Readable does. The same in verse 30.

decisions.choice: waandishi (L, B); walimu wa sheria (R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Literal and Balanced keep the title, "waandishi"; Readable says what these men were, experts in the law (meaning decision m1), as the English Readable does. The same in verse 30.

source.text: τίς δύναται ἁμαρτίας ἀφεῖναι εἰ μὴ μόνος ὁ θεός;

records.literal_gloss: Who is able sins to forgive except alone the God?

en.L: Who is able to forgive sins except God alone?"
en.B: Who has the power to forgive sins? Only God!"
en.R: Only God can forgive sins!"

es.L: ¿Quién es capaz de perdonar pecados, si no es solo Dios?».
es.B: ¿Quién tiene poder para perdonar pecados? ¡Solo Dios!».
es.R: ¡Solo Dios puede perdonar pecados!».

sw.L: Nani anaweza kusamehe dhambi, ila Mungu pekee?"
sw.B: Ni nani aliye na uwezo wa kusamehe dhambi? Mungu peke yake!"
sw.R: Mungu peke yake ndiye anayeweza kusamehe dhambi!"

decisions.choice: who can forgive sins but God alone: the teaching of the Scriptures
alternatives: a rule of their own making
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures it is God who blots out sins (Isaiah 43:25) and forgives wrongdoing (Exodus 34:6-7; Psalm 103:3). They are right that only God forgives; the question is who Jesus is (5:24).

decisions.choice: a statement
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer "no one"; Readable states it.

source.text: ἐπιγνοὺς δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Τί διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν;

records.literal_gloss: Having known and the Jesus the reasonings of them, answering he said to them, Why are you reasoning in the hearts of you?

en.L: But Jesus, knowing their reasonings, answered and said to them, "Why are you reasoning in your hearts?
en.B: Jesus was aware of what was going through their minds, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} replied, "Why do you debate this in your hearts?
en.R: Jesus knew what they were thinking. So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Why are you having such thoughts?

es.L: Pero Jesús, conociendo los razonamientos de ellos, respondiendo, les dijo: «¿Qué {{plural_you:razonan|razonáis}} en {{plural_you:sus|vuestros}} corazones?
es.B: Jesús se dio cuenta de lo que pensaban y les respondió: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:discuten|discutís}} esto en {{plural_you:su|vuestro}} corazón?
es.R: Jesús sabía lo que estaban pensando. Por eso les dijo: «¿Por qué {{plural_you:piensan|pensáis}} esas cosas?

sw.L: Lakini Yesu, akiyatambua mawazo yao, alijibu, akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnahojiana mioyoni mwenu?
sw.B: Yesu alijua yaliyokuwa yakipita mawazoni mwao, akawajibu, "Mbona mnajadiliana hivi mioyoni mwenu?
sw.R: Yesu alijua walichokuwa wakifikiri. Basi akawaambia, "Kwa nini mnawaza mambo kama hayo?

decisions.choice: knowing: knowing fully, seeing into their thoughts
decisions.reason: Luke shows Jesus knowing what people think (6:8; 9:47), something people expected of a prophet (7:39).

decisions.choice: in your hearts: in your minds
decisions.reason: In the Bible the heart is where a person thinks and decides.

decisions.choice: answering: Jesus answers what they had not said aloud
decisions.reason: Luke uses "answered" for Jesus replying to their thoughts.

decisions.choice: in your hearts (B); not rendered (R)
decisions.reason: Readable leaves out the picture, which in modern English suggests feelings.

source.text: τί ἐστιν εὐκοπώτερον, εἰπεῖν· Ἀφέωνταί σοι αἱ ἁμαρτίαι σου, ἢ εἰπεῖν· Ἔγειρε καὶ περιπάτει;

records.literal_gloss: Which is easier, to say, Have been forgiven to you the sins of you, or to say, Rise and walk?

en.L: Which is easier, to say, 'Your sins have been forgiven you,' or to say, 'Rise and walk'?
en.B: Which is easier to say: 'Your sins stand forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?
en.R: Is it easier to say to this man, 'Your sins are forgiven,' or to say, 'Get up and walk'?

es.L: ¿Qué es más fácil, decir: “Te han sido perdonados tus pecados”, o decir: “Levántate y camina”?
es.B: ¿Qué es más fácil decir: “Tus pecados quedan perdonados”, o “Levántate y camina”?
es.R: ¿Es más fácil decirle a este hombre: “Tus pecados están perdonados”, o decirle: “Levántate y camina”?

sw.L: Lipi lililo rahisi zaidi, kusema, 'Zimesamehewa kwako dhambi zako,' au kusema, 'Inuka, utembee'?
sw.B: Ni lipi rahisi zaidi kusema: 'Dhambi zako zimesamehewa,' au 'Simama, utembee'?
sw.R: Je, ni rahisi zaidi kumwambia mtu huyu, 'Dhambi zako zimesamehewa,' au kumwambia, 'Simama, utembee'?

decisions.choice: which is easier to say: the question compares saying the two things
decisions.reason: Anyone can say "your sins are forgiven", since no one can see whether it happened. Saying "get up and walk" is tested at once. Jesus will do the second to show that the first is true (5:24).

decisions.choice: to this man
decisions.reason: Readable says to whom the words are spoken.

source.text: ἵνα δὲ εἰδῆτε ὅτι ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου ἐξουσίαν ἔχει ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἀφιέναι ἁμαρτίας εἶπεν τῷ παραλελυμένῳ· Σοὶ λέγω, ἔγειρε καὶ ἄρας τὸ κλινίδιόν σου πορεύου εἰς τὸν οἶκόν σου.

records.literal_gloss: That but you may know that the Son of the Man authority has on the earth to forgive sins, he said to the [one] paralyzed, To you I say, rise and having taken up the little bed of you go to the house of you.

en.L: But so that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on the earth to forgive sins," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "I say to you, rise, and take up your little bed and go to your house."
en.B: But to show you that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins," {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to the paralyzed man, "I tell you, stand up, take your bed, and go off to your house."
en.R: But I will prove to you that the Son of Man has the right to forgive sins here on earth." Then Jesus said to the man who could not move, "I tell you, get up! Pick up your mat and go home."

es.L: Pero para que {{plural_you:sepan|sepáis}} que el Hijo del Hombre tiene autoridad en la tierra para perdonar pecados» —dijo al paralítico—: «A ti te digo: levántate y, tomando tu camilla, vete a tu casa».
es.B: Pero para que {{plural_you:vean|veáis}} que el Hijo del Hombre tiene autoridad en la tierra para perdonar pecados» —le dijo al paralítico—: «A ti te digo: ponte de pie, toma tu camilla y vete a tu casa».
es.R: Pero {{plural_you:les|os}} voy a demostrar que el Hijo del Hombre tiene derecho a perdonar pecados aquí en la tierra». Entonces Jesús le dijo al hombre que no podía moverse: «Te digo: ¡levántate! Toma tu camilla y vete a casa».

sw.L: Lakini ili mjue kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka duniani kusamehe dhambi," alimwambia yule aliyepooza, "Nakuambia wewe, inuka, na ukichukua kitanda chako kidogo, nenda nyumbani kwako."
sw.B: Lakini ili mwone kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka duniani ya kusamehe dhambi," alimwambia yule aliyepooza, "nakuambia, simama, chukua machela yako, uende nyumbani kwako."
sw.R: Lakini nitawathibitishia kwamba Mwana wa Adamu ana mamlaka ya kusamehe dhambi hapa duniani." Kisha Yesu akamwambia yule mtu asiyeweza kujisogeza, "Nakuambia, simama! Chukua mkeka wako, uende nyumbani."

decisions.choice: the Son of Man: Jesus's name for himself, recalling Daniel 7:13-14
alternatives: a son of man: simply a human being
decisions.reason: In Hebrew "son of man" can mean simply a human being (Psalm 8:5; Ezekiel 2:1). In Daniel 7:13-14 one like a son of man receives authority and everlasting rule from God. In the Gospels Jesus uses the title of himself. This is its first use in Luke.

decisions.choice: authority: the right and the power to act
decisions.reason: The noun means authority given and the power to use it (4:32, 36). Jesus claims the right to do what the scribes said belongs to God alone (5:21).

decisions.choice: on the earth: here and now, among people
decisions.reason: The Son of Man forgives sins now, on earth, not only when God judges.

decisions.choice: the sentence breaks off as Jesus turns to the man
decisions.reason: Jesus begins speaking to the scribes and Pharisees and finishes by speaking to the paralyzed man. Matthew and Mark have the same break (Mark 2:10).

decisions.choice: the Son of Man, with capitals and no gender setting
decisions.reason: A title, as in John 1:51, so it is never under the gender setting.

decisions.choice: I will prove to you; the right
alternatives: so that you may know; authority
decisions.reason: Readable says what Jesus is about to do and uses a plain word for authority.

decisions.choice: el Hijo del Hombre, with capitals as a title
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: the title Jesus uses of himself, with the figure of Daniel 7 behind it (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: autoridad (L, B); derecho (R)
decisions.reason: The word means both the right and the power to act (meaning decision m2). Each level follows the English word for it; Spanish has no single word that holds both.

decisions.choice: Mwana wa Adamu
decisions.reason: The settled Swahili title, used in John and across the New Testament drafts (meaning decision m1). "Mwana wa Mtu" is closer to the Greek words; a reviewer may weigh it.

decisions.choice: mamlaka at every level
decisions.reason: The word means both the right and the power to act (meaning decision m2). Where the English Readable says "the right", Swahili keeps "mamlaka", which holds both; "haki" is kept for righteousness.

source.text: καὶ παραχρῆμα ἀναστὰς ἐνώπιον αὐτῶν, ἄρας ἐφ’ ὃ κατέκειτο, ἀπῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον αὐτοῦ δοξάζων τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: And immediately having stood up before them, having taken up on which he was lying, he went away to the house of him glorifying the God.

en.L: And immediately he stood up before them, took up what he had been lying on, and went away to his house, glorifying God.
en.B: Right away the man stood up in front of them, picked up the bed he had been lying on, and went home giving glory to God.
en.R: The man got up at once while everyone watched. He picked up the mat he had been lying on. Then he went home, giving glory to God.

es.L: Y al instante, levantándose delante de ellos, tomó aquello en que estaba acostado y se fue a su casa glorificando a Dios.
es.B: Enseguida el hombre se puso de pie delante de ellos, tomó la camilla en la que había estado acostado y se fue a su casa dando gloria a Dios.
es.R: El hombre se levantó en ese mismo momento, mientras todos miraban. Tomó la camilla en la que había estado acostado. Luego se fue a su casa dando gloria a Dios.

sw.L: Na mara akisimama mbele yao, akichukua kile alichokuwa amelalia, aliondoka kwenda nyumbani kwake akimtukuza Mungu.
sw.B: Mara moja yule mtu alisimama mbele yao, akachukua machela aliyokuwa amelalia, akaenda nyumbani kwake akimtukuza Mungu.
sw.R: Yule mtu alisimama mara moja, watu wote wakimtazama. Akachukua mkeka aliokuwa amelalia. Kisha akaenda nyumbani akimtukuza Mungu.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he had done
decisions.reason: People in Luke give glory to God when they see his work (2:20; 7:16; 13:13; 17:15).

decisions.choice: immediately, and took up what he had been lying on: the healing is complete
decisions.reason: The man who was carried in on the bed now carries the bed.

decisions.choice: giving glory to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for glory; Balanced and Readable keep that word.

source.text: καὶ ἔκστασις ἔλαβεν ἅπαντας καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεόν, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν φόβου λέγοντες ὅτι Εἴδομεν παράδοξα σήμερον.

records.literal_gloss: And amazement seized all and they were glorifying the God, and were filled with fear saying that, We have seen extraordinary things today.

en.L: And amazement seized [them] all, and they were glorifying God, and they were filled with fear, saying, "We have seen extraordinary things today."
en.B: Everyone was overcome with amazement. They glorified God, and full of awe they said, "What we have seen today is beyond belief!"
en.R: Everyone was amazed, and they gave glory to God. They were full of fear and wonder. They said, "Today we have seen things we never thought could happen!"

es.L: Y el asombro se apoderó de todos, y glorificaban a Dios, y se llenaron de temor, diciendo: «Hoy hemos visto cosas extraordinarias».
es.B: Todos quedaron fuera de sí de asombro. Glorificaban a Dios y, llenos de reverencia, decían: «¡Lo que hemos visto hoy es increíble!».
es.R: Todos estaban asombrados y daban gloria a Dios. Sentían temor y admiración. Decían: «¡Hoy hemos visto cosas que nunca imaginamos que pudieran pasar!».

sw.L: Na mshangao ukawashika wote, nao wakawa wakimtukuza Mungu, wakajawa na hofu, wakisema, "Leo tumeona mambo yasiyo ya kawaida."
sw.B: Wote walishikwa na mshangao mkubwa. Wakamtukuza Mungu, na wakiwa wamejaa uchaji, wakasema, "Tuliyoyaona leo hayaaminiki!"
sw.R: Watu wote walishangaa, wakamtukuza Mungu. Walijaa hofu na mshangao. Wakasema, "Leo tumeona mambo ambayo hatukuwahi kudhani yangeweza kutokea!"

decisions.choice: amazement: astonishment that takes people out of themselves
decisions.reason: The noun can mean a trance (Acts 10:10), but here it is the overwhelming astonishment of the crowd.

decisions.choice: fear: awe before the power of God
decisions.reason: In Luke people are filled with fear when God acts among them (1:65; 7:16).

decisions.choice: extraordinary things: things beyond what anyone expected
decisions.reason: The word means what goes against all expectation.

decisions.choice: awe (B); fear and wonder (R)
decisions.reason: "Fear" alone would suggest terror; the meaning decision explains the sense.

source.text: Καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα ἐξῆλθεν καὶ ἐθεάσατο τελώνην ὀνόματι Λευὶν καθήμενον ἐπὶ τὸ τελώνιον, καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἀκολούθει μοι.

records.literal_gloss: And after these things he went out and saw a tax collector by name Levi sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, Follow me.

en.L: And after these things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at the tax booth, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: Later, Jesus went out and caught sight of a tax collector named Levi, seated at the place where he collected taxes. Jesus told him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: Later Jesus went out and saw a tax collector named Levi. Levi was sitting at the table where he collected taxes. Jesus said to him, "Follow {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}!"

es.L: Y después de estas cosas salió y vio a un publicano llamado Leví, sentado en el puesto de impuestos, y le dijo: «Sígueme».
es.B: Más tarde, Jesús salió y se fijó en un cobrador de impuestos llamado Leví, que estaba sentado en el lugar donde cobraba los impuestos. Jesús le dijo: «Sígueme».
es.R: Después Jesús salió y vio a un cobrador de impuestos que se llamaba Leví. Leví estaba sentado a la mesa donde cobraba los impuestos. Jesús le dijo: «¡Sígueme!».

sw.L: Na baada ya mambo hayo alitoka, akamwona mtoza ushuru jina lake Lawi ameketi kwenye kibanda cha ushuru, akamwambia, "Nifuate."
sw.B: Baadaye Yesu alitoka, akamwona mtoza ushuru mmoja aitwaye Lawi, ameketi mahali alipokuwa akitoza ushuru. Yesu akamwambia, "Nifuate."
sw.R: Baadaye Yesu alitoka, akamwona mtoza ushuru jina lake Lawi. Lawi alikuwa ameketi mezani alipokuwa akitoza ushuru. Yesu akamwambia, "Nifuate!"

decisions.choice: a tax collector at his booth: a man collecting tolls and taxes for the ruler
alternatives: a government official in an office
decisions.reason: Tax collectors were despised as cheats and as servants of foreign rulers (3:12). In Galilee they worked for Herod Antipas. Levi sat at a booth where tolls were paid, probably near Capernaum.

decisions.choice: Levi: the man called Matthew in Matthew 9:9
decisions.reason: Matthew's Gospel tells the same call with the name Matthew, and Luke lists a Matthew among the twelve (6:15). Mark calls him Levi son of Alphaeus (Mark 2:14).

decisions.choice: follow me: come with me as my disciple
decisions.reason: The same call as to the fishermen (5:11).

decisions.choice: the place (B) or table (R) where he collected taxes
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable describe the place.

decisions.choice: publicano (L); cobrador de impuestos (B, R)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts: Literal keeps the traditional name, "publicano"; Balanced and Readable say what the man did, which most readers no longer know from the old word. The same in verses 29 and 30.

decisions.choice: mtoza ushuru
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts, at every level: "one who collects duty", which says what the man did (meaning decision m1). The same in verses 29 and 30.

decisions.choice: Nifuate, with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The English "me" takes the setting. Swahili carries it in the object marker of the verb, which cannot take a capital.

source.text: καὶ καταλιπὼν πάντα ἀναστὰς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ.

records.literal_gloss: And having left all, having risen up he was following him.

en.L: And leaving everything, he rose up and followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He stood up, left it all, and began following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: Levi got up, left everything, and followed Jesus.

es.L: Y, dejándolo todo, se levantó y {{deity_pronoun:lo|Lo}} siguió.
es.B: Él se levantó, lo dejó todo y comenzó a seguirlo.
es.R: Leví se levantó, dejó todo y siguió a Jesús.

sw.L: Naye akiisha kuacha vyote, aliinuka, akawa akimfuata.
sw.B: Aliinuka, akaacha kila kitu, akaanza kumfuata.
sw.R: Lawi alisimama, akaacha kila kitu, akamfuata Yesu.

decisions.choice: he was following: he began to follow and went on following
alternatives: he followed for a short time
decisions.reason: The imperfect tense describes a following that continued.

decisions.choice: leaving everything: his work and its income
decisions.reason: Levi still has his house (5:29), but he leaves his post as a tax collector. The fishermen did the same (5:11).

decisions.choice: got up, then left everything
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable tell the actions in the order English expects.

source.text: Καὶ ἐποίησεν δοχὴν μεγάλην Λευὶς αὐτῷ ἐν τῇ οἰκίᾳ αὐτοῦ· καὶ ἦν ὄχλος πολὺς τελωνῶν καὶ ἄλλων οἳ ἦσαν μετ’ αὐτῶν κατακείμενοι.

records.literal_gloss: And made a feast great Levi for him in the house of him; and there was a crowd great of tax collectors and of others who were with them reclining.

en.L: And Levi made a great feast for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in his house, and there was a large crowd of tax collectors and others who were reclining [at table] with them.
en.B: Levi then gave a large feast at his house in honor of Jesus. A big crowd of tax collectors and other people were guests at the table with them.
en.R: Levi gave a big party at his house for Jesus. Many tax collectors and other people were there, eating with Jesus and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.

es.L: Y Leví {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} hizo un gran banquete en su casa; y había una gran multitud de publicanos y de otros que estaban recostados [a la mesa] con ellos.
es.B: Después Leví ofreció en su casa un gran banquete en honor de Jesús. Una gran multitud de cobradores de impuestos y de otras personas estaban a la mesa con ellos.
es.R: Leví hizo una gran fiesta en su casa para Jesús. Había allí muchos cobradores de impuestos y otras personas, que comían con Jesús y con {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.

sw.L: Na Lawi alimfanyia karamu kubwa nyumbani mwake; na palikuwa na umati mkubwa wa watoza ushuru na wengine waliokuwa wameegemea [mezani] pamoja nao.
sw.B: Kisha Lawi alimwandalia Yesu karamu kubwa nyumbani kwake. Umati mkubwa wa watoza ushuru na watu wengine walikuwa wageni mezani pamoja nao.
