sw.R: Lawi alimwandalia Yesu sherehe kubwa nyumbani kwake. Watoza ushuru wengi na watu wengine walikuwa pale, wakila pamoja na Yesu na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.

decisions.choice: a feast: a banquet with guests
decisions.reason: The word means a reception for guests (14:13).

decisions.choice: reclining: lying at table, as guests did at a feast
decisions.reason: At formal meals guests lay on couches around a low table, leaning on the left elbow (7:36-38).

decisions.choice: with them: with Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: The complaint in 5:30 is addressed to the disciples.

decisions.choice: with Jesus and his disciples
decisions.reason: Readable says who "them" are, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: guests at the table
decisions.reason: Balanced says what reclining meant without the unfamiliar custom.

decisions.choice: recostados [a la mesa]
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a feast (meaning decision m2). Literal keeps the posture and brackets the table, as Mark 2:15 does; Balanced and Readable say that they ate together.

decisions.choice: wameegemea [mezani] (reclining [at table])
decisions.reason: Guests lay on couches at a feast (meaning decision m2). "Kuegemea" is to lean or recline; Literal keeps the posture and brackets the table, as in Mark 2:15. Balanced and Readable say that they ate together.

source.text: καὶ ἐγόγγυζον οἱ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ γραμματεῖς αὐτῶν πρὸς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ λέγοντες· Διὰ τί μετὰ τῶν τελωνῶν καὶ ἁμαρτωλῶν ἐσθίετε καὶ πίνετε;

records.literal_gloss: And were grumbling the Pharisees and the scribes of them toward the disciples of him saying, Why with the tax collectors and sinners do you eat and drink?

en.L: And the Pharisees and their scribes were grumbling at {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, saying, "Why do you eat and drink with the tax collectors and sinners?"
en.B: This made the Pharisees and their own scribes grumble. They said to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples, "How can you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?"
en.R: The Pharisees and their teachers of the law did not like this. They complained to Jesus's disciples, "You eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners! Why do you do that?"

es.L: Y los fariseos y sus escribas murmuraban contra {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos, diciendo: «¿Por qué con los publicanos y pecadores {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}}?».
es.B: Esto hizo que los fariseos y sus propios escribas murmuraran. Les dijeron a {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos: «¿Cómo es que {{plural_you:comen|coméis}} y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} con cobradores de impuestos y pecadores?».
es.R: A los fariseos y a sus maestros de la ley no les gustó esto. Se quejaron a los discípulos de Jesús: «¡{{plural_you:Ustedes comen|Vosotros coméis}} y {{plural_you:beben|bebéis}} con cobradores de impuestos y pecadores! ¿Por qué lo {{plural_you:hacen|hacéis}}?».

sw.L: Na Mafarisayo na waandishi wao walikuwa wakiwanung'unikia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, wakisema, "Kwa nini pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi mnakula na kunywa?"
sw.B: Jambo hilo liliwafanya Mafarisayo na waandishi wao wenyewe kunung'unika. Wakawaambia wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, "Mnawezaje kula na kunywa pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi?"
sw.R: Mafarisayo na walimu wao wa sheria hawakupenda jambo hilo. Waliwalalamikia wanafunzi wa Yesu, "Ninyi mnakula na kunywa pamoja na watoza ushuru na wenye dhambi! Kwa nini mnafanya hivyo?"

decisions.choice: grumbling: the word used of Israel grumbling in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses this verb for Israel's complaints against Moses and God (Exodus 16:7-8; Numbers 14:27). Luke uses it again when Jesus welcomes sinners (15:2; 19:7).

decisions.choice: sinners: people known for breaking the law or living outside its rules
decisions.reason: The word marked out people whose way of life openly broke the law, and whom careful keepers of the law avoided (7:37, 39; 15:1-2).

decisions.choice: eat and drink with: sharing a table meant accepting people as companions
alternatives: only being in the same room
decisions.reason: To eat with someone was a sign of friendship. The Pharisees were careful about with whom they ate, to keep themselves ritually clean.

decisions.choice: their scribes: scribes who belonged to the Pharisees' party
decisions.reason: Not every scribe was a Pharisee; these were.

decisions.choice: teachers of the law (R); scribes (L, B)
decisions.reason: As in 5:21.

decisions.choice: a statement, then the question
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question into two short sentences.

decisions.choice: murmurar (L, B); se quejaron (R)
decisions.reason: "Murmurar" is the word Spanish readers know from Israel's grumbling in the wilderness, which this verb may recall (meaning decision m1). Readable uses the everyday word, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: kunung'unika (L, B); kulalamika (R)
decisions.reason: "Kunung'unika" is to grumble under one's breath, the word for Israel's grumbling in the wilderness, which this verb may recall (meaning decision m1). Readable uses the everyday word for complaining, as the English Readable does.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Οὐ χρείαν ἔχουσιν οἱ ὑγιαίνοντες ἰατροῦ ἀλλὰ οἱ κακῶς ἔχοντες·

records.literal_gloss: And answering the Jesus said to them, No need have the [ones] being healthy of a physician but the [ones] badly having;

en.L: And Jesus answered and said to them, "Those who are healthy have no need of a physician, but those who are sick [do];
en.B: "People who are well have no use for a doctor," Jesus answered them, "but people who are ill do.
en.R: Jesus answered them, "Healthy people do not need a doctor. Sick people need one.

es.L: Y respondiendo Jesús, les dijo: «No tienen necesidad de médico los que están sanos, sino los que están mal;
es.B: «Los que están bien no necesitan médico», les respondió Jesús, «sino los que están enfermos.
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Las personas sanas no necesitan médico. Los enfermos sí lo necesitan.

sw.L: Na Yesu akajibu, akawaambia, "Wenye siha hawahitaji tabibu, bali wale walio hali mbaya;
sw.B: "Watu walio wazima hawana kazi na daktari," Yesu aliwajibu, "bali wagonjwa ndio wanaomhitaji.
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu, "Watu wenye afya hawahitaji daktari. Wagonjwa ndio wanaomhitaji.

decisions.choice: the healthy have no need of a doctor: a proverb applied to Jesus's mission
decisions.reason: Jesus answers with a common saying. Like a doctor among the sick, he is among sinners because they are the ones who need him (5:32).

decisions.choice: those having badly: the sick
decisions.reason: "To have badly" is the Greek way of saying someone is ill (7:2).

source.text: οὐκ ἐλήλυθα καλέσαι δικαίους ἀλλὰ ἁμαρτωλοὺς εἰς μετάνοιαν.

records.literal_gloss: not I have come to call righteous [ones] but sinners to repentance.

en.L: I have not come to call righteous [people] but sinners to repentance."
en.B: The reason I have come is to call sinners to repentance, not the righteous."
en.R: I have not come to call people who are already right with God. I have come to call sinners to turn away from their sins and come back to God."

es.L: No he venido a llamar a [personas] justas, sino a pecadores, para el arrepentimiento».
es.B: He venido a llamar a los pecadores para que se arrepientan, no a los justos».
es.R: Yo no he venido a llamar a los que ya están bien con Dios. He venido a llamar a los pecadores para que dejen sus pecados y vuelvan a Dios».

sw.L: Sikuja kuwaita [watu] wenye haki, ila wenye dhambi, [waje] katika toba."
sw.B: Nimekuja kuwaita wenye dhambi ili watubu, wala si wenye haki."
sw.R: Sikuja kuwaita watu ambao tayari wako sawa mbele za Mungu. Nimekuja kuwaita wenye dhambi ili waache dhambi zao na kumrudia Mungu."

decisions.choice: the righteous: people who keep the law, or who think they do
alternatives: people who have no sin at all
decisions.reason: Jesus answers the Pharisees in their own terms. Luke shows elsewhere people who trusted that they were righteous and despised others (18:9).

decisions.choice: repentance: turning from sin back to God
decisions.reason: The word John used (3:3, 8). Only Luke has "to repentance" in this saying (compare Mark 2:17).

decisions.choice: call: invite, as to a meal
decisions.reason: The verb is used for inviting guests (14:16-17), which fits the setting at Levi's feast.

decisions.choice: I have come: Jesus speaks of his mission
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the purpose for which he came (19:10).

decisions.choice: people who are already right with God; to turn away from their sins and come back to God
decisions.reason: Readable explains both words.

decisions.choice: arrepentimiento (L); para que se arrepientan (B)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for turning from sin back to God (meaning decision m2). Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: toba (L); watubu (B)
decisions.reason: The term used across the New Testament drafts for turning from sin back to God (meaning decision m2). Readable says what it means, as the English Readable does.

source.text: Οἱ δὲ εἶπαν πρὸς αὐτόν· Οἱ μαθηταὶ Ἰωάννου νηστεύουσιν πυκνὰ καὶ δεήσεις ποιοῦνται, ὁμοίως καὶ οἱ τῶν Φαρισαίων, οἱ δὲ σοὶ ἐσθίουσιν καὶ πίνουσιν.

records.literal_gloss: They and said to him, The disciples of John fast often and prayers make, likewise also the [ones] of the Pharisees, the [ones] but yours eat and drink.

en.L: And they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "The disciples of John fast often and make prayers, and likewise also those of the Pharisees, but {{deity_pronoun:yours|Yours}} eat and drink."
en.B: Then they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "John's disciples fast frequently and offer prayers, and the Pharisees' disciples do the same. Yours, though, keep eating and drinking."
en.R: They said to Jesus, "John's disciples often fast, which means they go without food. They also say prayers. The Pharisees' disciples do the same. But {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} disciples eat and drink!"

es.L: Y ellos {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Los discípulos de Juan ayunan a menudo y hacen oraciones, e igualmente también los de los fariseos, pero los {{deity_pronoun:tuyos|Tuyos}} comen y beben».
es.B: Entonces {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} dijeron: «Los discípulos de Juan ayunan con frecuencia y hacen oraciones, y los discípulos de los fariseos hacen lo mismo. Los {{deity_pronoun:tuyos|Tuyos}}, en cambio, siguen comiendo y bebiendo».
es.R: Le dijeron a Jesús: «Los discípulos de Juan ayunan muchas veces, es decir, pasan tiempo sin comer. También hacen oraciones. Los discípulos de los fariseos hacen lo mismo. ¡Pero {{deity_pronoun:tus|Tus}} discípulos comen y beben!».

sw.L: Nao wakamwambia, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana hufunga mara kwa mara na kufanya maombi, vivyo hivyo pia wale wa Mafarisayo, lakini wale {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanakula na kunywa."
sw.B: Kisha walimwambia, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana hufunga mara nyingi na kuomba dua, na wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo hufanya vivyo hivyo. Lakini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanaendelea kula na kunywa."
sw.R: Walimwambia Yesu, "Wanafunzi wa Yohana hufunga mara nyingi, yaani, hukaa bila kula kwa muda. Pia husali. Wanafunzi wa Mafarisayo hufanya vivyo hivyo. Lakini wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}} wanakula na kunywa!"

decisions.choice: a statement: they said to him, "John's disciples fast", the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: a question: "Why do John's disciples fast ...?", the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Early manuscripts have a statement. Many later ones add "why", making it a question, as in Mark 2:18. The challenge is the same either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: they: the Pharisees and their scribes of 5:30
decisions.reason: Luke goes on with the same conversation at Levi's feast.

decisions.choice: fast: go without food for a time, as part of prayer or mourning
decisions.reason: The law set one day of fasting a year, the Day of Atonement (Leviticus 16:29). Many devout Jews fasted more; a Pharisee in one of Jesus's stories fasts twice a week (18:12).

decisions.choice: make prayers: pray regularly, perhaps at set times
decisions.reason: John taught his disciples a way to pray (11:1).

decisions.choice: which means they go without food
decisions.reason: Readable explains fasting.

source.text: ὁ δὲ εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Μὴ δύνασθε τοὺς υἱοὺς τοῦ νυμφῶνος ἐν ᾧ ὁ νυμφίος μετ’ αὐτῶν ἐστιν ποιῆσαι νηστεῦσαι;

records.literal_gloss: He and said to them, Not are you able the sons of the bridechamber, in which the bridegroom with them is, to make to fast?

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "You are not able to make the sons of the bridal chamber fast while the bridegroom is with them, are you?
en.B: He answered them, "Would you make the guests at a wedding fast while the bridegroom is still among them?
en.R: Jesus answered them, "When there is a wedding, the guests do not go without food while the bridegroom is with them. You could not make them do that!

es.L: Y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les dijo: «¿Acaso {{plural_you:pueden|podéis}} hacer ayunar a los hijos de la cámara nupcial mientras el novio está con ellos?
es.B: Él les respondió: «¿{{plural_you:Harían|Haríais}} ayunar a los invitados de una boda mientras el novio todavía está con ellos?
es.R: Jesús les respondió: «Cuando hay una boda, los invitados no dejan de comer mientras el novio está con ellos. ¡No {{plural_you:podrían|podríais}} obligarlos a hacer eso!

sw.L: Naye akawaambia, "Je, mnaweza kuwafanya wana wa ukumbi wa harusi wafunge wakati bwana harusi yuko pamoja nao?
sw.B: Aliwajibu, "Je, mngewalazimisha wageni wa harusi kufunga wakati bwana harusi bado yuko pamoja nao?
sw.R: Yesu aliwajibu, "Wakati wa harusi, wageni hawaachi kula wakati bwana harusi yuko pamoja nao. Hamngeweza kuwalazimisha kufanya hivyo!

decisions.choice: sons of the bridal chamber: the wedding guests, the bridegroom's friends
decisions.reason: "Sons of" is a Hebrew way of speaking about people who belong to something. These are the friends who celebrate with the bridegroom.

decisions.choice: the question expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The form of the question shows that no one would think of it.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a wedding was a time of feasting
decisions.reason: A wedding feast could last a week (Judges 14:12). Fasting belonged to mourning, so to fast at a wedding made no sense.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom: a picture of Jesus, recalling God as Israel's bridegroom
decisions.reason: The prophets picture God rejoicing over his people as a bridegroom over his bride (Isaiah 62:5; Hosea 2:19-20). John the Baptist calls Jesus the bridegroom (John 3:29). Jesus's presence is a time of joy.

decisions.choice: the guests at a wedding
alternatives: the sons of the bridal chamber
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the idiom.

decisions.choice: the bridegroom, lowercase and with no deity_pronoun span
decisions.reason: The bridegroom is a figure in a picture, as in John 3:29. Jesus speaks of himself through the picture without naming himself.

decisions.choice: los hijos de la cámara nupcial
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew-style idiom, as the English Literal does; it means the groom's friends and guests (meaning decision m1), and Balanced says so. "Hijos" here is the idiom, not a word about men, so it takes no gender span, as in Mark 2:19.

decisions.choice: wana wa ukumbi wa harusi
